sentences.text: The learned senior counsel for the Board along with learned counsel for the State seeks time for filing counter- affidavit.

The counter-affidavit of the Board shall with clarity record that as to whether the Math in question is a religious trust or not and if it is a religious, then whether it is registered with the Board or not and in the event, if it is registered with the Board, then why two registration numbers are there.

The counter-affidavit further shall also record that if the Math in question is registered with the Board as the religious trust, then whether the property of the trust in absence of Mahant with no successor in-line can be treated to be an escheat property or it is the duty of the Board to ensure that how such trust is to be managed.

The counter-affidavit further shall record with clarity that if the Math in question was a registered trust with the Board, then whether returns were being submitted by the Math in Patna High Court CWJC No.12121 of 2018(3) dt.09-05-2023 question to the Board or not and under what circumstances, permission was granted to the petitioner for selling land as is recorded in Annexure-6 to the writ application.
Further, the counter-affidavit shall specifically record about the genuineness of the Annexure-4, 5 and 6 appended to the writ application.

The counter-affidavit filed on behalf of the State shall be sworn by the District Magistrate,
Madhubani.
The counter-affidavit of the State shall with clarity record that on what basis, it was presumed that the property of the Math in question was an escheat property.

The counter-affidavit shall also record with clarity that as to why the petitioner was not given an opportunity of personal hearing thus breaching the order dated 30.01.2015 in C.W.J.C. No.995 of 1996 wherein this Court had clearly directed the Collector to pass orders after giving hearing to the petitioner.

The counter- affidavit of the State shall record with clarity that as to whether any notice was served upon the petitioner before taking the decision impugned in the present writ application or not apart from giving parawise reply to the writ Patna High Court CWJC No.12121 of 2018(3) dt.09-05-2023 application.

The counter-affidavit on behalf of the State shall also with clarity record that if dispute had arisen with respect to registration of the trust in question whether the Collector was competent to decide the same when it is the case of the Religious Trust Board that the Math in question is registered as Religious Trust with the Board.
Further, the counter- affidavit shall also bring on record the notification of 1983 by which the property of the Math in question is said to be an escheat property.

sentences.text:
The learned senior counsel for the petitioner, at this stage, submits that the present writ application has been filed seeking quashing of the order dated 22.02.2018 passed by the Collector, Madhubani,
which is in breach of the order passed by this Court in C.W.J.C. No.995 of 1996.

It is next submitted that the Math in question is a registered Math and the Mahant of the Math was Ram Kishor Das and after his death, the petitioner being his Chela was next in succession Patna High Court CWJC No.12121 of 2018(3) dt.09-05-2023 and thus, became the Mahant of the Math.

It is further submitted that the District Administration for the purposes of constructing a stadium forcefully took possession of some part of the land of the Math on the ground that after the death of Ram Kishor Das, there was no successor in-line, as such, the Math property in question in the Year 1983 was declared as an escheat property to which the petitioner had objected necessitating filing of C.W.J.C.
No.995 of 1996 in which, this Court had clearly directed the Collector to pass orders afresh after giving hearing to the petitioner and had also restrained the Collector from proceeding ahead with the construction of the stadium in question.

The learned senior counsel for the petitioner further submits that the District Administration apart from taking possession of the land of the Math in question had also taken possession of lands of private raiyats i.e. private respondents herein for the purposes of constructing the stadium in question.

It is further submitted that since the land of the private respondents was also taken, as such, in order to compensate them, instead of giving monetary Patna High Court CWJC No.12121 of 2018(3) dt.09-05-2023 compensation, the District Administration directed to compensate them by giving land of the Math on the ground that it is an escheat property.
The learned senior counsel for the petitioner next submits that the Collector by his order dated 22.02.2018 has already taken a decision to compensate the private respondents by the land of the Math.

The learned senior counsel for the petitioner submits that though in the order impugned, it has been recorded that the private respondents be compensated with the land of the Math in question, but then till date the said decision has not been acted upon.
It is thus prayed that the order impugned to that extent it directs for compensating the private respondents by the land of the Math be stayed.

The learned counsel for the State objects to the prayer made by the learned senior counsel for the petitioner on the ground that he has no instruction as to whether the land in question of the Math has been handed over to the private respondents in lieu of compensation for taking their land for construction of the stadium in question or not to Patna High Court CWJC No.12121 of 2018(3)
dt.09-05-2023 which the learned senior counsel for the petitioner submits that he has instruction to make submissions from the petitioner that the land of the Math till date has not been handed over to the private respondents.

Be that as it may, if the land of the Math till date has not been handed over to the private respondents in terms of the order dated 22.02.2018, passed by the Collector, Madhubani, then the Vishnu Kant Das vs The Bihar State Board Of Religious Trust ... on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80651536/
